comments.body:
Adjacent measured evidence from the lock-hold instrumentation on [rebar:7084-4e33-e698-42dd] (2026-08-07). Not a new root cause for this ticket, but it bears on how often the undeliverable-warning path is entered.

The tickets-branch push has a SECOND way to go pending that is not a rejected push at all: `push.py`'s merge leg acquires the store write lock with a **15s** budget (`_PUSH_MERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `attempts=1`) and, on LockTimeout at `push.py:355`, gives up and leaves the push PENDING with only a WARNING — the `tickets branch push-retry merge skipped: write lock busy; push stays pending` line already recorded on 7084.

Measured: a single `compact-on-close` holds that same lock for **48.1s** on a 7-event ticket and for **over 20 minutes** on a 75-event one (99% of it a per-event `git log --full-history` walk inside the critical section; see 7084 for the profile). A 15s budget cannot survive that. So under ordinary parallel-agent load the push-pending state is reached routinely by lock contention, not only by a declining remote — and on the async / library / MCP paths this ticket covers, that WARNING is discarded exactly the same way. The two defects compound: contention makes push-pending common, and this ticket makes it invisible.

Nothing implemented; the compaction remediation is proposed and awaiting operator approval on 7084.

comments.body:
# MCP limb CONFIRMED end-to-end (AC2, first half) — it was static evidence, now it is measured

The ticket flagged limb 3 (MCP) as "static evidence; this limb was not driven end-to-end and
should be confirmed first". Done, against a REAL rejecting origin — no mocks.

Drive: a real `rebar_repo` store; its tracker's `origin` repointed at a real local bare repo whose
real `pre-receive` hook declines with GH013-shaped stderr; `origin/tickets` seeded first so the
shape is a diverging branch, not a first push. Then the MCP server was built in-process
(`rebar.mcp_server.build_server()`) and the `comment_ticket` tool invoked through
`srv.call_tool(...)` — the same path a writing agent takes.

```
=== MCP comment_ticket RESULT ===
([TextContent(type='text', text='ok', annotations=None, meta=None)], {'result': 'ok'})
=== unpushed commits origin/tickets..HEAD: 2
```

**CONFIRMED, not refuted.** The tool returned the literal `ok` — both as text content and as the
FastMCP-derived structured `{"result": "ok"}` — while the push had really been declined and two
ticket commits were stranded locally. The writing agent reads only this result, so on the MCP
surface the failure is undeliverable exactly as limb 1 (async) and limb 2 (library) are. The
server-side `install_stderr_handler` does fire, but it writes to the SERVER's stderr, which the
agent never sees.

This also fixes the shape of the remedy for the `-> str` write tools: FastMCP ALREADY advertises
them as a generic `{result: <str>}` ack, so adding `push_status` alongside `result` is a strict
superset of the shape agents see today, not a new envelope.

Proceeding to implement the approved B4 remedy (durable marker + MCP `push_status` field) on
worktree `lamb-push-status`.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
# Implementation complete on worktree `lamb-push-status` — three design corrections worth recording

The approved B4 remedy is built: `src/rebar/_store/push_state.py` (a durable marker), recorded at
`push.py`'s single `_raise_if_strict` choke point, exposed as `rebar.push_status()` and as a
`push_status` field on every MCP write-tool result. 16 new tests, all driving a REAL local bare
origin with a REAL declining `pre-receive` hook.

**Mutation-checked, so the tests are not tautologies.** Removing the one `record_failure` line
turns exactly the 5 behaviour tests RED (and leaves the 5 contract-guard tests green, as they
must be); removing the two `clear` calls turns only the marker-clears test RED. Each half of the
fix is independently pinned.

## Three corrections the drive forced — each caught by a real failure, not by review

**1. The marker belongs in the tracker's GIT DIR, not its working tree.** My plan (D2) said a
dot-file beside the events, following `.ensure-hinted`. That was wrong, and two existing held-out
tests said so: `test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout` pins that a failed push leaves the
tracker's `git status` BYTE-IDENTICAL. `push.py` sets a dirty working tree aside (stash-commit ->
merge -> restore) to reconcile a non-fast-forward, so a marker in the working tree perturbs
exactly the state that dance operates on — and would show up as an untracked file in every store
on earth. It now lives in the git dir, resolved without a git subprocess and following a linked
worktree's `gitdir:` pointer. That makes "can never be committed or pushed" structural rather
than merely conventional.

**2. Deliberately NO `.json` suffix.** `test_push_rejection_surfacing` asserts "no event was
written" via `tracker.rglob("*.json")`, and rglob descends into the git dir. Rather than weaken a
held-out guard whose intent is sound, the artifact is named so nothing scanning for a ticket
event can miscount it.

**3. `remote-not-found` / `invalid-destination` are NOT delivery failures.** Measured: with them
recorded, EVERY local-only store — an explicitly supported mode, which `push.py` skips on purpose
— reported `state=pending, reason=remote-not-found` forever. That is the alarm-fatigue failure
mode that would have made this fix worse than the defect. They join `push-disabled` and
`async-delivery-unobservable` in `NON_FAILURE_REASONS`: the set of "no push was ever attempted".

## One scope REDUCTION vs the plan

D5 proposed minting a canonical `write_ack.schema.json`. It is not needed and was not added: the
ten `-> str` write tools become one shared `WriteAckOut {result, push_status}` — a strict superset
of the `{result: <str>}` FastMCP already advertised — and both the MCP schema-drift gate and the
output-schema coverage test pass with them still classified as generic acks. A canonical schema
pins a CLI/library `--output json` shape, and these acks are MCP-only (`rebar comment` prints no
JSON document), so minting one would have asserted a contract that does not exist. The exemption
reasons were updated to describe the new shape truthfully.

`declare_no_file_impact` keeps its documented `structured_output=False` exemption and so carries
no field; it is the one write tool that advertises no schema at all.

## Gates

`make lint` green (incl. the complexity baseline — the MCP helpers are module-level, not nested,
which kept `register_write_tools` at its ceiling of 29), `make typecheck` green (503 files), MCP
schema-drift gate green, output-schema coverage green (36), `docs/mcp-reference.md` regenerated
with no drift, and every touched module under the 800-LOC cap (`push.py` 786 — it SHED
`_unpushed_summary` to `push_state`, so this change made it smaller, not larger).

Full unit + interfaces suite running now; Gerrit next.

# LLM-Review -1 on 1639 was `bugfix-size-attestation` — attestation now EARNED (plan review PASS, signed)

Change 1639 got **Verified +1** (CI green) but **LLM-Review -1**, with one blocking finding:
`bugfix-size-attestation` — 483 non-test lines against the 150-line floor for a bug, and this
ticket held no plan-review attestation. Per policy the remedy is to EARN the attestation, not to
shrink the diff, so I ran `rebar review-plan`.

**It blocked four times before passing, and every block was a genuine gap in the plan rather than
gate noise.** The code was never the problem — in each case the plan text failed to state a
decision the implementation had already made. Fixed in order:

1. **P4 oversize (deterministic)** — the description was 8333 chars against the 8000 admission
   limit. Trimmed to 7999; the measured evidence it shed is preserved in the comments above and on
   2a76, so nothing was lost.
2. **AC1 raced the detached child (E6/E2)** — AC1 said the test asserts the marker exists "after
   the detached child exits", but the child is `start_new_session=True` and deliberately NEVER
   waited, so nothing said HOW the test synchronizes. The test already polls the marker path on a
   bounded 60s/0.1s deadline; AC1 now states that poll IS the synchronization contract for this
   limb, so the assertion is deterministic rather than racy.
3. **D5 undercounted the write tools (E4/G1G2)** — the plan said "the ten `-> str` tools"; there
   are **eleven**. Verified against the pre-change file: 11 match `) -> str:`. The eleventh,
   `declare_no_file_impact`, is `structured_output=False` and pinned in `NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT` by
   `test_no_schema_exempt_set_is_accurate`, so it advertises no outputSchema to extend and
   migrating it would regress that guard. The implementation already excluded it; the plan now
   says so and names it as the one documented gap.
4. **D4 was silent on the commit-phase reasons (G6)** — the choke point also carries
   `stage-failed` / `commit-failed` / `commit-lock-timeout` and the recovery reasons, which D4's
   four-item non-recorded list did not mention. Those ARE recorded, deliberately: a write that
   never got COMMITTED also never reached the remote and is invisible on the same surfaces, so
   `pending` plus a `reason` naming the phase beats silence. That decision was already in
   `record_failure`'s docstring; it is now in the plan too.
5. **Limb 4 had no AC (E6/E1/COH)** — the reconciler was diagnosed but unverified. Added **AC7**:
   it is fixed STRUCTURALLY, not by a fourth code path, because `push_state` records to disk
   regardless of which logger root holds a handler — the sole reason limb 4 was mute — and that is
   pinned by the AC3 drive asserting recording works with NO handler on the `rebar` root.

**Result: `review-plan` verdict PASS, attestation signed at head_sha `e78dadb4be`** — the same
commit as patchset 1, so the attestation is current for the change under review.

`rerun-llm-review` posted on 1639 with that rebuttal. No code changed, so CI stays green; awaiting
the re-vote.

compiled_state.description:
# A failed tickets push is UNDELIVERABLE on the async, library and MCP paths

RC-3 split out of bug 2a76-c9d9-4e8a-471b (closed), which fixed the CLI/synchronous path: the
terminal warning now names the git rejection reason and the backlog. This ticket covers the
surfaces where that warning is never DELIVERED at all, so 2a76's fix is a no-op for them.

## Proven at runtime (rebar-debug Phase 1; a real `pre-receive` decline, local bare origin)

1. **`sync.push = async`** — `push.py` re-spawns the push as a detached
   `Popen(..., stderr=DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)`, never waited, so every warning the child
   emits is discarded by the OS; only an `OSError` at SPAWN time is logged. MEASURED: against a
   rejecting hook → exit 0, stderr COMPLETELY EMPTY, backlog still incremented.
2. **Library embedders** — `rebar/__init__.py` attaches a `NullHandler` to the `rebar` root;
   `install_stderr_handler` runs only from the CLI and MCP server. MEASURED: in-process
   `rebar.comment(...)` → returned normally, stderr EMPTY, no push status in the return.
3. **MCP** — the handler targets the SERVER's stderr; the agent reads only the tool result.
   CONFIRMED end-to-end here (see comments): `comment_ticket` against a real declining origin
   returned `{"result": "ok"}` with two commits stranded.
4. **Reconciler subprocess** — installs its handler on the `rebar_reconciler` root while
   `rebar._store.push` logs under `rebar`, so its pushes are mute even in the foreground.

## Contract constraint (load-bearing)

`docs/concurrency.md` makes "a failed push never fails the caller" AUTHORITATIVE INTENT, pinned by
`push_tickets_branch`'s "ALWAYS returns None" and `tests/unit/test_store.py` (`# no raise`). The
remedy must be a SIGNAL, never an exception or a non-zero exit.

## Approved remedy (operator decision B4)

**An MCP `push_status` field on write-tool outputs plus a durable pending/unpushed marker.** OUT of
scope: changing CLI behaviour or any exit code, raising on the default path, and the
compaction/lock-contention work (tracked separately on 7084).

## Design

**D1 — new module `src/rebar/_store/push_state.py`.** `push.py` is at the hard 800-LOC cap, so the
new logic gets its own unit and `push.py` sheds `_unpushed_summary` into it (backlog counting IS
push state — an existing seam). Best-effort: every entry point swallows its own errors. API:
`record_failure` / `clear` / `read_status` → `{state: ok|pending, reason, detail, remote_ref,
unpushed, since}`.

**D2 — marker location.** The tracker's **git dir**, not its working tree. `push.py` sets a dirty
tree aside (stash-commit → merge → restore) to reconcile a non-fast-forward, and existing tests pin
that a failed push leaves the tracker's `git status` byte-identical — a working-tree marker
perturbs exactly that state. The git dir also makes "can never be committed or pushed" structural:
a record that the remote is unreachable must not itself need the remote.

**D3 — where it is recorded.** Every terminal failure already funnels through the single
`_raise_if_strict(strict, reason, detail, base, remote_ref)` choke point carrying the closed set of
`PushDeliveryError` reasons, so recording happens there — no call site changes, no path missed.
That function's body is today a no-op unless `strict=True`; it becomes record-unconditionally,
raise-only-for-strict, so the default path (and the detached child, same function) records while
still returning `None`. That is what makes limb 1 observable despite `/dev/null` stderr. A
successful push clears the marker.

**D4 — which reasons are recorded.** The choke point carries the whole delivery taxonomy, so the
split is explicit. NOT recorded — the four meaning no push was ATTEMPTED: `push-disabled`,
`async-delivery-unobservable`, `remote-not-found`, `invalid-destination`; otherwise every
local-only store (a supported mode) reports pending forever, the alarm-fatigue failure that would
make this worse than the defect. RECORDED, deliberately, is everything else, including the
COMMIT-phase reasons (`stage-failed`, `commit-failed`, `commit-lock-timeout`) and the recovery ones
(`merge-recovery-blocked`, `push-multi-bundle-conflict`, `store-epoch-*`, `lock-timeout`,
`push-policy-declined`, `push-transport-failed`, `final-push-rejected`). A write that never got
COMMITTED also never reached the remote and is invisible on the same surfaces, so `pending` plus a
`reason` naming the phase beats silence; a later successful push clears it either way.

**D5 — surfaces.** `rebar.push_status()` for library embedders (no logging handler needed). For
MCP, a `push_status` field on write-tool results. `_mcp_writes.py` defines ELEVEN `-> str` write
tools: comment/edit/link/unlink/tag/untag/archive/compact `_ticket(s)`, `set_file_impact`,
`set_verify_commands` and `declare_no_file_impact`. TEN migrate to a shared
`WriteAckOut {result, push_status}` — a strict SUPERSET of the `{result: <str>}` FastMCP already
advertises. `declare_no_file_impact` is EXCLUDED: it is `structured_output=False` and pinned in
`NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT` by `test_no_schema_exempt_set_is_accurate`, so it advertises no outputSchema to
extend and migrating it would regress that guard; it keeps its bare `"ok"` — the one documented
gap. The typed models (`CreateResultOut`, `ClaimResultOut`, `SignResultOut`) gain the field, and
the schema-less dict tools (`transition_ticket`, `reopen_ticket`) get the key. The ten stay
classified as generic acks in `test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`, whose EXEMPT_GENERIC reasons
are updated. On the async path the guarantee is that a SUBSEQUENT write or read reports it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **async path observable.** With `sync.push=async` against a real bare origin whose
      `pre-receive` hook declines, a write leaves a durable marker naming the reason. The child is
      detached with `start_new_session=True` and deliberately NEVER waited, so the test cannot join
      it: it synchronizes by POLLING the marker path on a bounded deadline (≤60s, 0.1s interval),
      failing if the deadline elapses. That poll is the synchronization contract for this limb, so
      the assertion is deterministic, not racy. Before the fix: no marker, empty stderr.
- [ ] AC2 — **MCP limb confirmed, then fixed.** First driven END-TO-END through the MCP
      `comment_ticket` tool against the rejecting origin and its result inspected (recorded as a
      comment); the result then carries `push_status` state `pending` naming the reason, asserted
      by a test on the MCP surface.
- [ ] AC3 — **library limb.** `rebar.push_status()` returns `state == "pending"` with the reason
      after an in-process `rebar.comment(...)` whose push was really rejected, with NO logging
      handler installed — asserted by a test driving a real rejecting remote.
- [ ] AC4 — **the marker clears.** After the remote stops declining and a later write pushes
      successfully, the marker is gone and status reports `ok` — asserted by a test, so the signal
      cannot latch permanently.
- [ ] AC5 — **best-effort contract preserved.** `push_tickets_branch` still returns `None`, never
      raises on the default path, no CLI exit code changes, and an unwritable marker does not fail
      the write. Regression-asserted.
- [ ] AC7 — **reconciler limb (limb 4) covered by the same mechanism.** Fixed STRUCTURALLY, not by
      a fourth code path: `push_state` records to disk regardless of which logger root holds a
      handler — the sole reason limb 4 was mute. Pinned by asserting recording works with NO
      handler on the `rebar` root (the AC3 drive), so it cannot regress to logger-dependent. No
      separate reconciler integration test is in scope.
- [ ] AC6 — **gates green.** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the MCP output-schema coverage test, the
      schema drift gate, the mcp-reference drift gate and the module-size gate all pass; the change
      is `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1` on Gerrit before this ticket closes.
